item.title: Australia Seeks Global Alliance to Fight Big Tech on Child Harms
item.description: Australian Communications Minister Anika Wells is working to form a worldwide coalition of nations to press tech giants such as Meta Platforms Inc. to reduce online harm, potentially opening a new front in a widening regulatory battle against the industry.
item.dc:creator: Angus Whitley

item.title: SpaceX Earnings Live: Updates on SPCX 3Q 2026 Results, Elon Musk Comments
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Democrats Warn Tech CEOs Over Election Disinformation
item.description: Senior Democratic lawmakers warned the chief executives of the largest US technology firms that their platforms were failing to crack down on disinformation spread by Russia and other actors on their platforms ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Natalia Drozdiak

item.title: Four-Minute Transfers Upend How Money Moves
item.description: Bloomberg's Katherine Schwartz joins joins Scarlet Fu and James Seyffart on "Bloomberg Crypto." Western Union and MoneyGram are adopting crypto technology to defend their businesses and deepen customer ties. Their money transfer time has gone from three days to as short as four minutes. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: JPMorgan Brings JPM Coin To Ether For Clients
item.description: Bloomberg's Anna Irrera joins joins Scarlet Fu and James Seyffart on "Bloomberg Crypto." JPMorgan Chase is launching its deposit token on Ether, extending the lender’s push into blockchain payments. JPM Coin — which represents US dollar deposits at the largest US bank — will be made available to the company’s institutional clients on the Ethereum network. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Redefining Market Leaders With New Finance: Kaul
item.description: Sandy Kaul, head of innovation at Franklin Templeton, joins Scarlet Fu and James Seyffart on "Bloomberg Crypto." They discuss Franklins efforts to modernize various parts of the financial system. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Seeing Some AI-To-AI Crypto Commerce: Jardine
item.description: Eric Jardine, head of research at Chainalysis, joins Scarlet Fu and James Seyffart on "Bloomberg Crypto." They discuss the research from Chainalysis that found AI agents are spending crypto autonomously, making more than 138 million crypto transactions on Base, the most popular blockchain for agentic commerce. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Business As Usual After Liquid Hack: Back
item.description: Adam Back, co-founder & CEO Blockstream, joins Scarlet Fu and James Seyffart on "Bloomberg Crypto." The Liquid Network, a Bitcoin-linked blockchain started by Blockstream in 2018, was hit by a $320 million hack that drained about 4,000 Bitcoin. The hackers, who claimed to be so-called white hats exposing security flaws in the network, later returned some of the Bitcoin. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Gut Check, Inside Citadel's Securities Conference
item.description:
Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." AI gets a gut-check as a data-center debut crashes on valuation and debt fears. GM tightens its profit outlook and launches a $20 billion buyback. Plus, Dani Burger live from Citadel’s Future of Global Markets Conference with Scott Rubner, Jim Esposito and Konstantine Buhler on AI, markets and what’s next.
Correction: This video was edited to correct the name of the firm, Sequoia Capital, that aired at 10:40 a.m. ET. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI's Next Frontier: The Agent Economy
item.description:
AI isn't just changing how we work, it may be creating an entirely new economy. Sequoia Capital Partner Konstantine Buhler joins Dani Burger at Citadel's Securities Conference to explain why he's bullish on AI agents, job growth, and long-term investing and why today's market shifts won't erase tomorrow's opportunities.
Correction: This video was edited to correct the name of the firm, Sequoia Capital, that aired at 10:40 a.m. ET. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Z.AI Founds Worked with Accused Chinese Spy Group
item.description: Four founders from one of China's up-and-coming AI companies, Z.AI, worked on a study that was funded by a group accused of having ties to Chinese spies. Bloomberg's Kate O'Keeffe explains the tech and national security concerns with Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ASI’s Buckendorf on Winning FAA, Military Deals
item.description: ASI founder and CEO Phillip Buckendorf explains how the company’s AI helps customers like the FAA and military orchestrate complex systems and how it beat out rivals including Palantir to win government contracts. Buckendorf discusses how the company plans to use the $325 million it just raised at a $3 billion valuation, with Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Fears Roar Back After Elice IPO Flop
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down why fears about the AI trade are resurfacing after South Korean data center firm Elice plunged 32% in its market debut. Plus, Anthropic is in talks with Nscale for a massive new computing deal that could be worth as much as $45 billion, and Eric Schmidt's early Anthropic bet could pay off big, with a stake worth as much as $20 billion if Anthropic hits a $2 trillion IPO valuation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Eric Schmidt’s Early Anthropic Bet Set to Pay Huge Windfall
item.description: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt owns around 1% of Anthropic thanks to his early investment in the startup, setting him up for one of the largest individual windfalls from the company’s imminent public market debut. Bloomberg's Natasha Mascarenhas joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: NScale, Anthropic in Talks for $45B AI Computing Deal
item.description: Anthropic is in talks with Nscale for a massive new computing deal that could be worth as much as $45 billion. The deal would be for a second facility at Nscale's Monarch data center campus in West Virginia, which would deliver 460 megawatts of computing power using Nvidia's advanced Vera Rubin AI chips. Bloomberg's Bailey Lipschultz joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta’s Chief Global Affairs Officer Joel Kaplan Departing
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. Chief Global Affairs Officer Joel Kaplan is leaving after spending years steering the company through its most tumultuous political moments.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra S. Levine

item.title: ASI Hits $3 Billion Valuation in $325 Million Funding Round
item.description: Startup ASI raised $325 million in new funding from investors, allowing the company to expand an artificial intelligence system that helps the military, airlines and air-traffic controllers manage assets.
item.dc:creator: Ed Ludlow and Rebecca Torrence

item.title: Salesforce Fills Marketing Hole With $5.7 Billion Deal for Braze
item.description: Salesforce Inc. plugged a gap in its marketing platform with an agreement to buy Braze Inc. for an enterprise value of about $5.7 billion, aiming to add more artificial intelligence features to products that were increasingly seen as outdated.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford and Dana Wollman

item.title: Google Cloud Outage Mostly Resolved After Knocking Out Services
item.description: A Google Cloud outage in Europe that knocked out digital bank Revolut Ltd. and other online services for several hours on Tuesday has mostly been resolved, the US tech company said.
item.dc:creator: Shona Ghosh and Charlie Wells

item.title: US Sanctions Chinese Venture Firm in Google AI Secrets Case
item.description: The US government has blacklisted a Chinese venture firm established by ex-Microsoft Corp. AI scientist Lu Qi for alleged ties to a startup accused of stealing technology from Alphabet Inc.’s Google.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
